source.title: A meta-analytic review of moral licensing

confidence_rationale: This is the human behavioural analogue of MECH-023's B-prime control, and it is included because it cuts BOTH ways. It supports the non-Markovian half decisively -- present moral behaviour depends on moral history at a matched present situation, d = 0.31 across 91 studies and 7,397 participants. But the effect as characterised is DOMAIN-GENERAL moral-self-image accounting, which is much closer to the 'global cost shift' alternative MECH-023 names as a falsifier than to region-shaped geometry. Confidence is held at 0.55 because the meta-analysis itself reports publication status as the only supported moderator and calls the literature underpowered.
failure_signatures: The licensing effect is generally reported ACROSS domains -- a prior good deed in one domain licenses transgression in an unrelated one -- which is the signature of a scalar moral-credit ledger, not of a path-shaped terrain. If REE's residue produced the same divergence for the A and B-prime forks, MECH-023 would be falsified by its own criterion (ii); the human literature's default finding sits on the falsifying side.

Sign is opposite to residue: licensing predicts that a GOOD history makes subsequent transgression MORE likely, whereas REE's residue predicts that a HARM history makes subsequent harm-adjacent commitment LESS likely. The two effects can coexist in humans (licensing and cleansing are both reported) but a single scalar residue term cannot produce both, so the architecture may be modelling only one arm of the human phenomenon.

Publication status was the only moderator with support and published studies showed larger effects; the authors state the primary studies are underpowered for moderator detection. The domain-generality conclusion is therefore itself uncertain, which is the one respect in which this entry's challenge to MECH-023 is weaker than it looks.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Across 91 studies and 7,397 participants, people who have initially behaved morally are subsequently more likely to display immoral, unethical or otherwise problematic behaviour (Cohen's d = 0.31). Publication status was the only moderator with empirical support; the authors conclude that primary studies are substantially underpowered for moderator analysis.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-023 asserts that responsibility is path-dependent and non-Markovian. Moral licensing is the most robust human demonstration that moral decisions are not a function of the present situation alone -- two people facing an identical choice diverge according to what they did earlier. That is criterion (i) in human behavioural form. But the licensing literature also characterises the mechanism as a domain-general moral self-concept or moral-credential account, in which the history contributes a scalar to a self-image ledger. In REE terms that is a global cost shift, and MECH-023 explicitly names the global-shift outcome as FALSIFYING: if fork A and fork B-prime (equal harm mass, distant region) diverge identically, the geometry is not path-shaped.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Two transfers are doing heavy lifting and both are contestable. First, human moral self-image involves explicit narrative self-report and social accountability, neither of which REE's residue field has; the mechanisms may be homologous in effect and unrelated in kind. Second, the DIRECTION is inverted -- licensing runs from good history to subsequent transgression, residue runs from harm history to subsequent avoidance. The moral-cleansing literature supplies the matching direction, but the meta-analysis here covers licensing specifically, so the sign match is asserted by analogy rather than measured. Read this entry as a sharpening of MECH-023's own falsifier, not as support for it.
mapping.source_context: Meta-analysis of laboratory and field studies of human moral behaviour, predominantly Western undergraduate and online samples.

confidence_components.notes: Mapping fidelity is deliberately low: what the meta-analysis measures (self-image accounting over explicit moral acts) and what MECH-023 measures (residue-weighted candidate ranking at a matched latent state) share a shape and not a substrate. High transfer risk is the point of including it -- it names the alternative hypothesis the REE design must beat.
